status.en: 203 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 21% fewer than the week before, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 203 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 21 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to target civilians in Plateau, killing a 60-year-old woman harvesting groundnuts and injuring two farmers, while Fulani attackers killed a farmer and wounded another. In Taraba, bandits have killed dozens of villagers, with reports of 52 bodies buried and later 58 bodies recovered from a market attack, and also struck near Sokoto University. Northern senators are demanding the arrest and prosecution of the perpetrators of the Taraba attacks. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å angripe sivile i Plateau, og drepte en 60‑år gammel kvinne som høstet jordnøtter og såret to bønder, mens Fulani-angripere drepte en bonde og såret en annen. I Taraba har banditter drept dusinvis av landsbyboere, med rapporter om 52 lik begravd og senere 58 lik funnet etter et angrep på et marked, og de rammet også i nærheten av Sokoto-universitetet. Nordlige senatorer krever arrestasjon og rettsforfølgelse av gjerningspersonene i Taraba-angrepene. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
